items.title: 15.5.2 Peripheral Nervous System - Cranial & Spinal Nerves

source_refs.note: Topic 15.5.2 with the table of cranial nerves (PDF 40-42); Figure 15.15 is redrawn as an original diagram beside the table, and Figure 15.16 is drawn as an original diagram after the list of spinal nerves.

blocks.text: The peripheral nervous system consists of nerves and ganglia. Nerves are cable-like collections of axons. Ganglia are aggregations of cell bodies located outside CNS. The nerves which arise from brain are called cranial nerves while those which arise from spinal nerves are called spinal nerves

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book prints “those which arise from spinal nerves are called spinal nerves”. It should read: those which arise from the spinal cord are called spinal nerves.

There are 12 pairs of cranial nerves. The first two pairs of cranial nerves (olfactory nerve and optic nerve) arise from cerebrum. The other 10 cranial nerve pairs arise from the brainstem. Some of cranial nerves are sensory, some are motor and others are mixed nerves (contain axons of sensory and motor neurons).

blocks.alt: The underside of the brain with the twelve pairs of cranial nerves in different colours: the olfactory bulbs (CN-I) at the front, the optic nerves crossing (CN-II), and CN-III to CN-XII leaving the brainstem in order from the midbrain down to the medulla, with the cerebellum below.

rows: Movement of the superior oblique muscle of eye
Sensation in the face; control of the muscles involved in chewing
Movement of the lateral muscles of eye which are responsible for outward gaze
Facial expressions and the sense of taste in the front of the tongue.
Sense of taste in the back of tongue; movement of the muscles involved in swallowing
Controls many organs, including heart, lungs, and digestive system
Controls the muscles in the neck and shoulders
Controls the muscles of the tongue

blocks.text: There are thirty-one pairs of spinal nerves. All spinal nerves are mixed. They transmit sensory and motor information between the spinal cord and the rest of the body.

Each spinal nerve emerges from the spinal cord by two short branches or roots. The dorsal root contains the axons and dendrites of sensory neurons. The ventral root contains the axons of motor neurons. The two roots join just before a spinal nerve leaves the vertebral column. The cell bodies of sensory neurons are grouped together outside spinal cord in the dorsal root ganglia. The cell bodies of somatic motor neurons are located within the spinal cord and so are not located in ganglia. The 31 pairs of spinal nerves include;
